THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR HEARING ON 08.09.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 M.A.C.A.No.1017 of 2020  2  2025:KER:66655  C.S.SUDHA, J.
 -----------------------------------------------------------
 M.A.C.A.No.1017 of 2020  -----------------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 08th day of September 2025  JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.584/2011 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thrissur,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 08/11/2017.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 04/01/2011 at about 08:00 a.m., while he was riding motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-08-H-4669 through Thrissur Sahithiya Academy-Wadakechira road and when he reached in front of Wadakkechira main gate, bus bearing registration No.KL/08/AD/1800 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
The 1st respondent/owner and the 2nd respondent/driver remained ex parte.
4. The 3rd respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle.
The age, occupation and income were disputed.
It was also contended that the amount claimed was excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A1
to A11 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
Ext.B1 policy was marked on the side of the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on a consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the offending bus resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 5,28,000/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.

Jestin George vs Surendran on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77113854/
2 7.
The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal 2025:KER:66655 calling for an interference by this Court.

8. Heard both sides.
9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a 23 year old B.Tech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering was earning 25,000/- per month.
In order to establish the same, Ext.A9 appointment letter was produced.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 10,000/-, which is quite low and hence the same needs to be enhanced.

In support of the argument, he relies on the dictum of the Apex Court in Kandasami v. Linda Briyal, 2023 ACJ 1653, where the monthly income of an engineering graduate was fixed as 25,000/- per month, in which case the accident took place in the year 2008.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the claim petitioner on the date of the accident was not employed and hence the reason why the Tribunal was not inclined to rely on the materials produced by the claim petitioner and fix the notional income.

The 2025:KER:66655 income that has been fixed by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and if at all the Court is inclined to enhance the same, it may be fixed as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd, (2011) 13 SCC 236.
9.1.

sentences.text: In Ext.A9 appointment letter dated 12/12/2010 it is stated that the claim petitioner was on probation for a period of 3 months w.e.f. 31/12/2010.
The Tribunal was not inclined to rely on Ext.A9 as there was no evidence to show that the claim petitioner was continuing in the said Firm on the date of the accident.
However, the fact that the claim petitioner was a Network Engineer is not seen disputed.
His qualification has been established by Ext.A8 certificate and therefore his notional income can be fixed as 20,000/- per month.
Loss of earnings 10.
In the light of the nature of injuries sustained, which include fracture of the hip as well as on the right leg, in all probability, he might have been unable to work for a period of 9 months.
Hence, he can be awarded loss of earnings for 9 months, that is, 20,000/- x 9 months = 1,80,000/-.
Percentage of disability 11.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that based on Ext.A7 disability certificate, the Tribunal ought to have fixed the functional disability at 21%.
The doctor as per Ext.A7 has assessed the whole body disability at 21% and therefore the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the disability to 10% without assigning any reasons.
Therefore, he submits that the disability may be fixed as per Ext.A7 certificate.
On the other hand, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that Ext.A7 certificate has not been issued by a Medical Board.

On the other hand, it has been issued by a private doctor, who has not treated the claim petitioner and hence, in such circumstances, the functional disability fixed at 10% by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and does not call for any interference.

3 11.1.

The materials on record show that the claim petitioner, a young man aged 23 years sustained the following injuries- "Lacerated wound 30x15 cm on right leg, lacerated wound on right foot 15x5cm,
lacerated wound 1x0.5cm right forehead, two lacerated wounds right cheek, two lacerated wounds on upper and lower lips, pain right hip area, fracture tibia, fibula right leg, fracture superior+posterior wall acetabulam +post 2025:KER:66655 dislocation right hip, intra acetabular fragments + Fracture both bones right leg+soft tissue loss medial aspect right leg and Type IIIB open fracture right leg, degloving injury right leg with severe crush injury right leg muscles."
11.2. Ext.A7 Disability Certificate reads thus- " DISABILITY CERTIFICATE
This is to certify that I have examined sri.Jestin George, 28yrs, M, s/oGeorge, Adayal(H), Kannara on 2.10.15 for assessment of permanent physical disability.

I have verified the wound certificate (no26415,
dt.4.1.11), discharge summary and the fresh X-rays (no.678, dt.11.10.15) before issuing the certificate.
HE was an IT instructor by profession.

The patient gives a h/o road traffic accident on 4.1.11 following which he was admitted at Aswini hospital, Thrissur with fracture superior and posterior wall acetabulum(R) with posterior dislocation hip, fracture both bones(R) leg, soft tissue loss medial aspect (R) leg.
He was treated by operative fixation of the (R) tibia with ILN, (R) acetabulum with plate and screws alongwith other supportive measures and was discharged on 8.2.11.
The implants on the tibia and acetablulam are remaining in situ.

On clinicoradiological examination the patient has the following findings:
1. Ugly deformity, scarring and muscle contracture over the (R)leg 2.
Bony bowing over the (R) leg 3. Shortening of 1 inch (R)lower limb 4. Range of flexion of (R)knee (120)decreased than the (L)knee(130)

5. Range of dorsiflexion(10), plantar flexion(20) of (R) ankle decreased than (L)
ankle (DF-20,PF-30) 2025:KER:66655 6.
Surgical scar (R)gluteal region

7. Pain and difficulty over the hip on squatting, sitting cross- Jestin George vs Surendran on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77113854/
4 legged, climbing stairs and prolonged standing 8. Radiologically, malunited fracture both bones (R)leg, implants in situ, acetabulum fracture with implants in situ The whole body permanent disability has been calculated using Mcbride scale as follows:
% for fracture acetabulum(R) with partial ankylosis of the hip = 7% % for fracture both bones (R) leg with angulation =9% % for 1 inch shortening (R)lower limb = 5%
% for partial ankylosis of the (R)ankle with 10 dorsiflexion = 2% Combining the values using Kessler's formula, total% of disability = 21% Conclusion
sri. Jestin George has got 21(twentyone)% of permanent physical disability (whole body) with respect to his injuries sustained in the accident.
I have not treated this patient.
I have got more than 10yrs standing in orthopaedics."
It is true that the doctor who issued the certificate, had not treated the claim petitioner.
However, on going through the impugned Award, I find that Ext.A7 disability certificate was never objected to when it was admitted in evidence in support of the claim of the claim petitioner.
The injuries sustained include fractures to the hip as well as the right leg.
It also involves a severe crush injury as well as a degloving injury on the right leg.
It is pointed out that the work of a network engineer is not an exclusive desk job and that he has to move around for the discharge of his duties.

Therefore, in the light of the disabilities sustained which are referred to in Ext.A7 and in the light of the dictum in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343, the functional disability is fixed as 21%.

sentences.text: Pain and suffering 12.
An amount of 50,000/- was claimed.
However, the Tribunal awarded an amount of 30,000/-.
In the light of the injuries sustained, which include 3 fractures and the surgical interventions that he had to undergo, I find that an amount of 50,000/- as claimed can be granted under this head.
Loss of amenities 13.
An amount of 40,000/- was claimed.
The Tribunal granted an amount of 25,000/-.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that an amount of 40,000/- as claimed can be granted under this head.
The impugned Award is modified to the following extent :

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 8,46,200/- (total compensation =13,74,200/-, that is, 5,28,000/- granted by the Tribunal +
8,46,200/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the compensation amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.

Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
